content: For children aged 1 to 10 years, or children over 10 years but weighing less than 40 kg, the recommended dosage is 5 mg/kg orally once daily or every 12 hours, with a maximum dose not exceeding 150 mg per day. For children over 10 years of age and weighing more than 40 kg, the recommended dosage is 100 mg orally every 12 hours. In cases of severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance <10 mL/min) or liver impairment, the medication should be administered once daily. Rimantadine interacts with several medications and substances through pharmacodynamic synergism, which can enhance central nervous system (CNS) side effects. These include aclidinium, atropine (IV/IM), glycopyrrolate (inhaled), henbane, hyoscyamine spray, oxybutynin (oral and transdermal), and rapacuronium. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended when these combinations are used. Additionally, ublixtuximab may decrease the effects of rimantadine due to its immunosuppressive properties, increasing the risk of infection. Rimantadine increases the effects of aclidinium, atropine (IV/IM), glycopyrrolate (oral and inhaled), henbane, hyoscyamine spray, oxybutynin (oral and transdermal), and rapacuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of these interactions is considered minor or unknown, but monitoring is still advised. Common side effects of rimantadine include dizziness (2%), nervousness (1-2%), fatigue (1%), headache (1%), insomnia (2%), difficulty concentrating (<2%), anxiety (1%), anorexia (2%), weakness (1%), nausea (3%), vomiting (2%), dry mouth (2%), and abdominal pain (1%). Less common but more severe side effects include dyspnea, agitation, ataxia, tachycardia, tremor, convulsions, heart block, hyperkinesias, bronchospasm, gait abnormalities, and hypersensitivity reactions to amantadine, rimantadine, or any drug component. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) advises against the use of rimantadine for the treatment or prophylaxis of influenza in the United States during the 2008-09 influenza season. Caution is recommended in patients with a history of seizures, and the medication should be discontinued if seizures occur. Rimantadine should also be avoided in patients with active or uncontrolled psychosis and used cautiously in those with renal impairment. It is classified as Pregnancy Category C and enters breast milk. Rimantadine inhibits the replication of three subtypes of influenza A (H1N1, H2N2, H3N2) early in the viral replication cycle but has no activity against influenza B virus. The drug has a half-life of approximately 4 hours, which is prolonged in elderly patients and those with severe renal or hepatic impairment. Peak plasma levels are reached in 6 hours, and the drug is excreted in the urine, with less than 25% excreted as unchanged drug. Hemodialysis does not contribute to drug clearance. The above information is provided for general informational and educational purposes. Individual treatment plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. For the most current information, contact the applicable plan provider.
